hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext: My Skills delegated-wait exception: While supervising an active implementer, use a shared writable progress log and mailbox waits. Only the child writes progress entries; the parent communicates directly with the child. Every child direct message and final handoff specifies log-read: none when self-contained, or log-read: <absolute-path>:<start-line>-<end-line> with verified 1-based line numbers when log context is needed. The parent reads only the requested range; a message, completion, or timeout does not itself require a log read. If more context is needed and no range was supplied, ask the child for it. In this state, this instruction replaces the default requirements to provide commentary every 60 seconds and avoid waits longer than 60 seconds. Agree up front on milestones, immediate decision/blocker reporting, and a credible stall deadline. Choose a timeout up to the stall deadline, often about 30 minutes for substantial work, within the tool's maximum; a message or completion can end it early. Give an update before waiting. On a child decision or blocker message, follow its log-read instruction and reply directly with send_message for an active child or followup_task for the same idle child before waiting again; never just go back to sleep or record the parent's response in the log. On child completion, follow its log-read instruction, then begin acceptance. At the stall deadline, use the stall procedure without automatically reading the log. An empty timeout before that deadline calls directly for another wait. Outside delegated waiting, retain the normal communication guidance. This exception does not authorize delegation or change ownership, acceptance, writer settlement, or approval requirements.
